excerpts.text: Before 2022, Q/q and R/r were the only Latin letters available for abbreviations, with all other Latin letters either being: already used for other prefixes ([a](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atto- "Atto-"), [c](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centi- "Centi-"), [d](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deci- "Deci-"), [E](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exa- "Exa-"), [f](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Femto- "Femto-"), [G](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giga- "Giga-"), [h](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hecto- "Hecto-"), [k](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kilo- "Kilo-"), [M](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mega- "Mega-"), [m](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milli- "Milli-"), [n](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nano- "Nano-"), [P](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peta- "Peta-"), [p](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pico- "Pico-"), [T](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tera- "Tera-"), [Y](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yotta- "Yotta-"), [y](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yocto- "Yocto-"), [Z](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zetta- "Zetta-"), [z](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zepto- "Zepto-")); already used for [SI units](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SI_units "SI units") (including: [SI base units](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SI_base_unit "SI base unit"), [SI derived units](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SI_derived_unit "SI derived unit"), [non-SI units mentioned in the SI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-SI_units_mentioned_in_the_SI "Non-SI units mentioned in the SI"); [A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ampere "Ampere"), [B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bel_(unit) "Bel (unit)"), [C](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coulomb "Coulomb"), [d](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Day "Day"), [F](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farad "Farad"), [g](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gram "Gram"), [H](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_(unit) "Henry (unit)"), [h](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hour "Hour"), [J](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joule "Joule"), [K](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kelvin "Kelvin"), [L](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Litre "Litre"), [m](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metre "Metre"), [N](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newton_(unit) "Newton (unit)"), [S](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siemens_(unit) "Siemens (unit)"), [s](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second "Second"), [T](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla_(unit) "Tesla (unit)"), [t](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tonne "Tonne"), [u](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unified_atomic_mass_unit "Unified atomic mass unit"), [V](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volt "Volt"), [W](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Watt "Watt")); easily confused with mathematical symbols (I and l are easily confused with 1, O and o are easily confused with 0, X and x are easily confused with ×); or a combination (some symbols are used for both, e.g. metre and milli- both use m).
